referents.why: Plural 'them' (autois) that Pilate answers. The plural addressed is the crowd of Mrk.15.8, but no plural candidate is offered.
Plural 'to you' inside Pilate's speech. The addressees are the crowd of Mrk.15.8, which is not a candidate.
Plural 'you' inside Pilate's wish. The crowd again, not a candidate.

links.why: Subjunctive 'I should release' is the object of the verb of wishing. Grammar nesting; not a verb of knowing or saying, so not 'that'.
links.category: object clause of a verb of wishing

links.why: Participle 'saying' is a manner role of the main verb 'answered'.
The participle governs the speech it introduces. Grammar nesting kept beside the content link.
R1: the saying participle introduces what is said (cl2).
Self-link; a clause is not 'and then' itself.

groups.why: Frame is the answering clause cl0. Part was cl1, the participle 'saying', which carries no content; what is said is cl2 (R1). Sender is Pilate (R2). The addressee is the crowd, which is not a candidate, so no addressee member is given.
groups.category: speech turn with addressee not in candidates

referents.why: 'Him' (auton), the one handed over by the chief priests out of envy: Jesus. The builder's Pilate does not fit, since the handing over is of Jesus.

referents.why: Third singular 'he knew' in a clause opened by gar. The knower is the one who asked in Mrk.15.9, Pilate.
referents.category: implied subject of a verb of knowing

links.why: Hoti after 'he knew': what is known. Verb of knowing.
Self-link.
Verse-opening gar is 'for': the reason for Pilate's offer to release Jesus in Mrk.15.9 is that he knew of the envy. The edge runs from the explained clause to its reason.

referents.why: 'To them' (autois) after 'release to': the ones Barabbas is released to are the crowd. The chief priests stirred the crowd and are not the recipients. The pronoun is plural but ochlos is singular and collective, so agreement is by sense.
Third singular subject of 'might release' in a purpose clause. The one who releases is the governor, Pilate. Barabbas is the one released (object), not the doer.
referents.category: implied subject of a purpose clause

links.why: Hina plus subjunctive, third person, after 'stirred up': what the stirring is for.
Self-link.

referents.why: 'To them' (autois) after 'was saying': the crowd, plural addressees. No plural candidate is offered.
Interrogative 'What' (Ti) as object of 'should do'. It asks for an action and names no referent; no neuter candidate.
Relative 'whom' (hon) in 'whom you call King of the Jews'. Its antecedent is 'Him' (Jesus), whose title is 'the King'; candidate w13 is that title.
referents.category: relative pronoun with antecedent named by title

referents.why: First singular in Pilate's question ('What I should do'). The speaker is Pilate.

Relative clause inside the object noun phrase 'Him'.

referents.why: 'Him' (auton) is the one the crowd calls to be crucified: Jesus. Jesus is not in this verse's candidate list, which offers only Pilate and Barabbas.
Implied 'you' of the imperative is the one the cry is spoken to: Pilate, who asked the question in Mrk.15.12. Singular morphology fits one addressee.

links.why: The command is the object of 'cried out'. Grammar nesting kept beside the content link.
R1: 'cried out' is a clause of calling out that introduces what is said: a single command, so the said clause itself.

referents.why: 'To them' (autois) after 'was saying': the crowd, plural. No plural candidate is offered.
Interrogative 'What evil' as object of 'did He commit'. Names no referent.
'Him' (auton), object of 'Crucify': Jesus. Not among the candidates. This verse has an empty before window, so Jesus named in Mrk.15.5 and Mrk.15.12 is not offered.
Implied 'he' of 'did He commit': Jesus, the one accused. Not among the candidates (see w14).
Implied 'you' of the command 'Crucify Him' is the one the crowd speaks to: Pilate, the questioner in this verse.

links.why: The question is the object of 'was saying'. Grammar nesting kept beside the content link.
R1: 'was saying' introduces the question.

R1: 'shouted' introduces what is said, the command.

The connective is Greek de ('but'), and cl2 sets the crowd's shout against Pilate's question. 'And then' does not carry that opposition.

referents.why: Subject of the purpose clause 'that he might be crucified' (hina plus subjunctive). The one flogged and handed over is Jesus. The builder's Pilate would make the one who is crucified the agent of it.

links.why: Participle 'desiring' is a role of the main verb.
Infinitive 'to satisfy' completes the participle 'desiring' (the object of wishing), not a purpose.
Participle 'having flogged' is a role of the main verb.
Hina plus subjunctive, third person: what the handing over is for.
Narrative sequence: the release is followed by the flogging and handing over. De kai continues the line of events.
The infinitive is nested inside the participle, not a next event; the narrative line runs cl0 then cl3.
